To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the primary action of insulin on the liver is indirect, mediated by the adipocyte; and 2) the primary reason for insulin's secretion into the portal vein is to allow the liver to be more insulin sensitive when the liver has become resistant to insulin's direct action.

insulin acts indirectly on the liver through non-esterified free fatty acid (NEFA) release from adipose tissue, that NEFA are a signal to the beta cell as well as a substrate, and that insulin resistance of the central adiposity pattern is compensated by a reduction in hepatic insulin extraction.
Insulin acts on the liver to suppress glucose output by a primary action on the adipocyte, and the portal route of administration is necessary to maintain insulin sensitivity of the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which insulin controls glucose homeostasis, and how these are altered by obesity.
the regulation of glucose production by the liver.
the role of non-esterfied fatty acids (NEFAs) as a signal to the insulin sensitive tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin's primary action in regulating glucose output from the liver is on the adipocytes, and that this effect is mediated by NEFA.
insulin is secreted into the hepatic portal vein to control glucose production by the liver.

(i) NEFAs have a major role in the regulation of glucose production; (ii) insulin is secreted into the hepatic portal vein because it is the only way to deliver insulin to muscle in adequate amounts to control blood glucose levels; (iii) the liver is insulin resistant because of the high portal vein NEFA concentration, but this is compensated for by a reduction of hepatic insulin clearance, so that more insulin is delivered to muscle, where it is effective in glucose uptake;
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
insulin resistance is a complex process, involving many tissues and multiple mechanisms.
the primary site of action for the insulin effect on glucose production is the adipocyte.
insulin resistance is a consequence of central obesity, which causes insulin resistance of the adipocyte.
The main takeaway from our work is that
insulin is not the direct regulator of glucose output from the liver.
insulin resistance in the liver can occur with central adiposity and is due to portal vein NEFA.
insulin resistance is not a disease.
